header.title: Bamberger Arzneibuch ['Arzenîbuoch Ipocratis' (B)] (Bamberg, Staatsbibl., Msc. Hist. 146 (früher E.VII.19)): AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Anonymous
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's urn:rem:anonymous:m015:norm, from the Referenzkorpus Mittelhochdeutsch, ReM 2.1 (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. Only some passages are translated so far: those that the Atlas of Ancient Myth, Magic in the Ancient Texts and the demons-and-angels study cite.

notes.2v.8: 2v.16–17 seem garbled: under anderhalp is read as unde anderhalp, 'and on the other side'; schoz is the shot, the arrowhead or missile lodged in the wound. bunge is probably brooklime (Veronica beccabunga). ôrgemint may be orpiment. halgalia is probably galangal. harz bech may be a single item, 'resin-pitch'.
notes.1r.1: 1r.1 holds only the initial D and alle; the opening words of the sentence (probably 'he had') are missing. Promodosius (Promodosio) is unidentified. 1r.14 kinne may be 'cheeks' or 'jaws'. 1r.19 obe read as 'or'.

his books to be laid in his grave under his head.
Long afterwards an emperor passed by there, and
supposed that great treasure was inside. Then
he had the [grave] [opened], and found in it
[a] book, all his medicine. Then he took the book and
would give it to no one except the physician
Promodosius. When he searched the book, he found first of all
in it, concerning headache, [this] manner: When a
person has [the] ache and [the] swelling in the
face without the cough, and if [he] often lays [the] left hand
on his breast, [and] [if] [he] often scratches [his] nose, [then] he dies
on the 23rd [day]. When, in the man who is
phrenetic, both [the] cheeks redden, with frequent panting,
and he cannot digest, then he dies on the
9th day. This disorder very often [has] the cold sweats
and the cold ears and the cold teeth. Whoever
has aching neck veins, and if he is as one who
is deaf, and if the white spot troubles him, or the other
spots, and if he craves the warm bath or sweating, then
he dies on the 50th day. Here begins the book of Hippocrates.
Here begins the medical book of Hippocrates, which [he] wrote
[against] all the sicknesses that can arise in
all the human limbs. For pain in the head.
three measures of wine, and boil it in a new pot, and
let it cool, and give it to the sick person for three days while he is fasting,
and tell him to walk about afterwards. Item, for the spleen:
take the middle bark of the sallow, a handful,
and boil it in a new pot with last year's
wine down to the third part, and press it very well
out, and give it for three days to the one whose spleen aches. If
you want to test this, give it to a
pig to drink, and on the other side, opposite the wound,
the shot [the arrowhead] comes out. For healing a wound.
For the wound: take powdered *bunge* and sprinkle
it over the wound, and it heals. Give this same herb to the
wounded man to drink; if he vomits it, he dies.
This is a wonderful powder for healing wounds. Item,
